name: Publication governance for leaked-data and image attribution claims

attribution.legal_posture: Source-qualified investigative reporting and defensive abstraction; named-person attribution, nationality finding, and adjudicated legal fact remain unestablished.

caveats: The record uses source text only; facial recognition, image-similarity identity inference, and possible victim imagery stay outside publication.
Research and public exports contain source-bounded material; raw leaked data, private selectors, credentials, communications, and victim details stay outside them.
Reporting may be close to operations, while public sources leave the evidentiary material unsuitable for revalidation and republication.

statements: Use this behavior or governance pattern only with corroborated, consistently applied human review.
limitations: No single accent, ethnicity, nationality, appearance, camera or audio quality, geography, address, payment service, remote-work preference, device-hosting request, or technical-answer anomaly establishes fraud or DPRK attribution.
Do not publish or derive legal identities, pseudonyms, stolen identities, victim details, private selectors, leaked communications, credentials, or image matches from these records.

statements: Researcher-attributed faces, online CVs, private communications, and leaked operational records should remain leads unless an official source or independently verifiable public record supports the identity and relationship claimed.
limitations: The reporting may be close to operations, but the evidentiary material cannot be safely revalidated or republished from public sources alone.
No facial recognition, image-similarity identity inference, or publication of possible identity-theft victims.
No raw leaked data, private selectors, credentials, communications, or victim details in research or public exports.
